solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Actor Bogart shaking with rage

indicators.note: shaking things up jumbles them, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Humphrey Bogart trembles with fury on set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaking' rearranges BOGART and RAGE together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star, so a performer of the screen.

clue.text: Bloody good men — last in infantry

parts.note: OR stands for 'other ranks', soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: 'last in' points to the final letter of the word infantry

explanation.surface: A grim battlefield report about the rear rank of foot soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gory and bloody are synonyms, both describing a scene full of blood and violence.

clue.text: Puts a stop to English nudist regularly getting stripped

indicators.note: the word nudist is stripped of every other letter, keeping a regular alternate sequence

explanation.surface: A naturist keeps undressing, until someone calls a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to stop it, so the verb matches 'puts a stop to'.

clue.text: A good one might make chap shoot par!

definitions.text: A good one might make chap shoot par!

indicators.note: the letters might be made into a new word, signalling a rearrangement of the three words

explanation.surface: A golfer's well-struck shot to the green could earn him par on the hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: 'might make' rearranges CHAP SHOOT PAR, and a good shot of this kind lets a golfer make par.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, the stroke played towards the green from the fairway; a good one sets up a par.

clue.text: Top quality oil stirred into dressing

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook stirs the finest oil into a salad dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI, the digit 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise, a sauce or dressing from Provence.

clue.text: Yeoman's ale containing iron consumed

definitions.note: read as 'Yeoman is': the definition is the yeoman, the 's a link

indicators.note: the beer holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
ate means consumed, eaten

explanation.surface: A Yeoman Warder downs his ale after a hearty meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Yeoman's reads as 'Yeoman is', the 's acting as a link. 'containing' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yeomen Warders of the Tower of London are nicknamed this, so a yeoman of the guard.

clue.text: Continental chap seen in vermeille every now and again

indicators.note: taking letters every now and again means picking alternate ones from vermeille

explanation.surface: A European man spotted in a gilt finish here and there.
explanation.walkthrough: Vermeille is gilded silver; the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a German or Scandinavian male first name, so a man from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Met Al up in Ambleside about upcoming work

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the concealed letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
about here means around, in the vicinity of: the letters lie within the words Met Al up in Ambleside

explanation.surface: Bumping into a friend called Al on a trip to the Lake District town of Ambleside.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambleside is a town in England's Lake District. 'about' hides the letters across the words and 'upcoming' reverses them, read upwards in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To work something can mean to handle or control it skilfully, as to manipulate does.

clue.text: Research facility in which question of political leaning is asked?

definitions.meaning: a building where scientists run experiments

definitions.text: in which question of political leaning is asked?
definitions.meaning: the question '...?' asks which of the two big UK parties someone favours

explanation.surface: A building where people are quizzed about how they vote.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as LAB OR A TORY, the word becomes a question about voting Labour (Lab) or Conservative (Tory), Britain's two main parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab is a place equipped for scientific experiments and research.

clue.text: Embarrassed editor hiding base gambit assigned elsewhere

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces conceals the others between them

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red
e is the base of natural logarithms
a gambit is a ploy, a cunning move

explanation.surface: A red-faced editor hides a trick and gets moved to another post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' is the insertion signal; the editor splits the colour from its abbreviation. 'base' is the mathematical constant e, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeploy staff or troops is to move them to a new task or place.

clue.text: Ignore small Greek character… bye!

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a bye

explanation.surface: Someone cold-shoulders a minor Greek figure and waves goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball, marked B.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub a person is to rebuff them, pointedly ignoring them.

clue.text: Morse completely stumped, unable to start the crossword

definitions.meaning: the TV detective Inspector Morse, baffled by a case with no leads
a solver who can't get going has no idea where to begin, lacking any hint

explanation.surface: Even the crossword-loving Inspector Morse can't make a start on today's puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: Morse, the Oxford detective of novels and TV, is famous for doing crosswords, which joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means completely baffled, and literally a detective with no leads or a solver with no hints.

clue.text: Sexually explicit British epic period novel Romeo?

definitions.text: Sexually explicit British epic period novel Romeo?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of epic period are put in a new order

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Is a racy British historical saga about a lover worth reading?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer while also building it. 'novel' rearranges EPIC PERIOD between B and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is slang for a steamy historical romance novel full of seduction.

clue.text: Identify gamble covering weak investment climate

indicators.note: the wager wraps around the other piece, covering it

parts.note: a bet is a gamble or wager
to earmark something is to set it aside or single it out

explanation.surface: Picking out a bet to hedge against a falling stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' signals insertion; 'Identify' is the verb meaning to set aside for a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: On the stock exchange, a period of falling share prices and pessimism is called this.

clue.text: Sanction old registered trademark "Bottled Potpourri"

indicators.note: bottled up means held inside, so the approval holds the other pieces

parts.note: assent is approval or sanction
R is the abbreviation for registered, as in the circled R mark
TM is the trademark symbol

explanation.surface: Approval for an old branded scent sold in bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottled' signals insertion; the quoted brand name in the surface hides that Potpourri is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A potpourri is a mixed collection of things, a medley or miscellany.

clue.text: Each way price laid about a side of Great Britain?

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way

indicators.note: the price is laid around the A, enclosing it

parts.note: cost means price

explanation.surface: A betting slip: each-way odds placed on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each way' looks like a racing bet but is two abbreviations. 'laid about' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The eastern seaboard is one coastline of Great Britain, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Throw up some confetti for Pat Archer, making hay

indicators.note: in a down entry, throwing up means sending the letters upwards, read in reverse
some of the letters of confetti for Pat Archer are taken, concealed across the words

explanation.surface: Tossing confetti at a wedding for Pat Archer of the radio soap The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio farming soap; Pat Archer is a character. 'some' hides the letters and 'Throw up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: To make hay (while the sun shines) is to exploit an opportunity and earn well, trading in profit.

clue.text: He's enthralled by the lottery

definitions.note: read as 'he is': the definition is the man himself, a serf

indicators.note: held captive by the words the lottery, the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A man captivated by the national draw.
explanation.walkthrough: Enthralled also hints at the answer's sense: a helot was in thrall, a serf in ancient Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf of ancient Sparta, so a man in bondage.

clue.text: Test batsman, opener from Somerset, becomes established

parts.note: Joe Root is an England Test cricket batsman

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter of Somerset

explanation.surface: A batsman from the county side Somerset beds in at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: Test cricket is the international form; Somerset is an English county cricket side, and 'opener' (also an opening batsman) gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that roots takes hold in soil, so something that becomes settled and established.

clue.text: Instrument invented by plucky performer?

parts.note: an imaginary instrument, made up by someone who mimes strumming; plucky hints at plucking strings

explanation.surface: A brave musician has dreamed up a new instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plucky' suggests courage but means plucking strings; 'invented' means imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names miming a rock guitarist's moves with an imaginary instrument.

clue.text: Reprise Cleopatra in new year

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of Cleopatra in

explanation.surface: Staging Cleopatra again to mark the new year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges CLEOPATRA IN, with Y added.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay of a sports highlight on TV repeats it, as a reprise repeats music.

clue.text: Spanish chap game to get infusion of different blood type?

indicators.note: the game receives a transfusion of another group, swapping out one O, itself a blood group

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
AB is one of the human blood groups

explanation.surface: A Spanish player needs a transfusion of a different blood group.
explanation.walkthrough: One O in POLO, read as blood type O, is replaced by AB, a different blood type.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo is a common Spanish male first name, as in Picasso.

clue.text: Indigo metal block (5 down)

indicators.note: the five goes down, dropped out of the block

parts.note: an anvil is a heavy iron block used by smiths
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A dye-stained iron block, with a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '(5 down)' looks like a cross-reference but is wordplay: Roman 5, V, is taken out of ANVIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Stand up to democratically elected Free Yemen leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the four words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A political slogan urging a newly elected Yemeni government to be free.
explanation.definitionFit: To defy someone is to resist or confront them openly.

clue.text: Capital that is outwardly grand. Very

indicators.note: the two pieces sit on the outside of the other

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, a grand
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A city that looks magnificent on the outside, very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' puts K and V around IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now often spelt Kyiv, is the capital city of Ukraine.

clue.text: Somewhat unstable, Oscar leaves money in the bank

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ff is the abbreviation for folios, leaves of a book
your balance is what is in your account

explanation.surface: A shaky fellow named Oscar departs, leaving cash on deposit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun: pages, abbreviated ff (folios).
explanation.definitionFit: Being slightly out of equilibrium, wobbly or unsteady, matches somewhat unstable.

clue.text: Going around French State Gallery

indicators.note: going around means turning back, so the French word is reversed

parts.note: état is French for state; the run of letters inside the English word State is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A tour around the French state's art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tate is the famous London art museum, with branches like Tate Modern.

clue.text: Some golf kept royals busy

indicators.note: busy suggests activity and bustle, so the letters of kept royals are shuffled

explanation.surface: A round on the links kept the royal family occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'busy' rearranges KEPT ROYALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf scored by counting every shot taken, as against match play by holes won.
